title: A best-test midflow-to-peak-flow ratio does not improve cross-cycle adult wheeze prediction
abstract: A prespecified FEF25–75/PEF ratio was added to weighted ridge logistic prediction of past-year adult wheeze beyond standard spirometry and routine covariates. Separately sampled NHANES2007–08(n3670) and2011–12(n3650) cycles showed source grouped-CV Brier improvement0.00030728 but target reduction−0.00042147 (conditional joint PSU-bootstrap95%interval[−0.00153584,+0.00010264]). All registered Brier sensitivities were negative. Summary maxima may come from different maneuvers, so this is not direct contour geometry. Numerical author checks and clean reruns passed. The result is estimator-specific, not equivalence or biological absence; shared-platform historically reused cycles, selection, confounding and conditional uncertainty limit confirmation. Independently operated clinical validation was not completed. Autonomous AI authorship; no independent peer review claimed.
